en.name: Lemon juice, fresh squeezed
en.summary: Freshly squeezed lemon juice keeps 6 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 12 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F). It is far more acidic than most juices, which is why it outlasts them in the fridge — but it is still raw, unpasteurised juice.
en.pantry: No room-temperature timeline is given for fresh lemon juice, and there should not be one. The acidity keeps most bacteria at bay, but the juice is raw, it carries whatever was on the skin of the fruit, and left warm it loses its aroma within hours and turns bitter as the oils from the pith oxidise. Squeeze it into a clean jar and refrigerate it straight away.
en.fridge: 6 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a small, clean, tightly closed jar filled as full as you can manage. The less air above the juice the better, because oxidation is what dulls the flavour first — day-old fresh lemon juice is already noticeably less bright than the juice you squeezed this morning. Strain out the pips and pulp if you want the longest window; pulp carries more of the enzymes that turn the flavour.
en.freezer: 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F), and this is the answer for anyone who squeezes a bag of lemons at once. Freeze it in an ice-cube tray, then bag the cubes: one cube is roughly a tablespoon, which is what most recipes want. Leave headspace in any container, because juice expands as it freezes. The flavour survives freezing far better than it survives a week in the fridge.
en.thawing: Thaw cubes in the fridge, or drop them straight into a hot pan, a dressing or a drink. Do not leave juice to thaw at room temperature.
spoilage: Mould on the surface or around the rim of the jar.
A cloudy, ropey or slimy look where the juice was simply hazy.
A flat, bitter or fermented smell instead of a sharp citrus one.
Fizzing, which means something has started to ferment.
tips: Freeze in ice-cube trays; one cube is about a tablespoon.
Fill the jar to the top so there is as little air as possible above the juice.
Strain out pulp and pips for the longest fridge window.
Zest the lemons before juicing and freeze the zest separately; it is worth more than the juice.

faq.q: How long does fresh lemon juice last?
faq.a: 6 days in the fridge at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, or 12 months in the freezer at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Can you freeze fresh lemon juice?
faq.a: Yes, 12 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Ice-cube trays are the practical way, and the flavour holds up well.

faq.q: Why does fresh lemon juice taste different the next day?
faq.a: Oxidation dulls the bright top notes within hours, and pulp enzymes push it towards bitterness. It is still good for days, just less vivid.

zh.name: 現榨檸檬汁
zh.summary: 現榨檸檬汁放 4 °C 以下冷藏可放 6 天，−18 °C 冷凍可放 12 個月。它的酸度比多數果汁高得多，所以在冰箱裡也撐得比較久——但它終究是生的、未殺菌的果汁。
zh.pantry: 現榨檸檬汁沒有室溫的期限數據，也不該有。酸度擋得住大部分細菌，但這是生的果汁，帶著果皮上原有的一切；放在溫暖處，香氣幾小時內就散掉，白膜裡的油脂氧化後還會轉苦。請擠進乾淨的罐子，立刻冷藏。
zh.fridge: 用小而乾淨、蓋緊的罐子，盡量裝滿，放 4 °C 以下冷藏 6 天。汁液上方的空氣越少越好，因為最先讓風味變鈍的就是氧化——放了一天的現榨檸檬汁，明顯已經沒有早上剛榨時那麼明亮。想要最長的窗口，就把籽和果肉濾掉；果肉帶著比較多會改變風味的酵素。
zh.freezer: −18 °C 下 12 個月；一次擠一整袋檸檬的人，答案就是這個。用製冰盒凍成小塊再裝袋：一塊大約是一大匙，正好是多數食譜要的量。任何容器都要留膨脹空間，因為果汁結凍會變大。風味撐過冷凍的能力，遠比撐過冰箱裡那一週來得好。
zh.thawing: 冰塊請放冷藏解凍，或直接丟進熱鍋、沙拉醬或飲料裡。不要放在室溫退冰。
spoilage: 原本只是略帶混濁的果汁變得濃濁、牽絲或黏滑。
聞起來平板、發苦或有發酵味，而不是明亮的柑橘酸香。
出現氣泡，代表有東西開始發酵。
tips: 用製冰盒分裝冷凍；一塊大約一大匙。
罐子裝滿到頂，讓上方的空氣越少越好。
濾掉果肉和籽，冷藏的窗口會最長。
榨之前先把皮刨下來分開冷凍，檸檬皮屑的價值比汁還高。

faq.q: 現榨檸檬汁可以放多久？
faq.a: 4 °C 以下冷藏 6 天，或 −18 °C 冷凍 12 個月。

faq.q: 現榨檸檬汁可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 可以，−18 °C 下 12 個月。用製冰盒最實際，風味也保持得很好。

faq.q: 為什麼現榨檸檬汁隔天味道就不一樣？
faq.a: 氧化會在幾小時內把明亮的前段香氣磨掉，果肉裡的酵素也會把它往苦味推。它還能放好幾天，只是沒那麼鮮明。
